sessions.task: Discovered + measured a real capacity collision: seedGoblins' out-of-sight placement fails against the toolkit's smaller canonical crypt dimensions for a material fraction of RandomSeed values (deterministic per seed) -- up to ~33% for a full 4-player party, on the real entropy-seeded path every production caller uses (no proto field carries a seed)
sessions.notes: Sweep evidence (real spatial/spawn/perception packages, no test doubles): party=1 9.7%/1000, party=2 11.9%/1000, party=3 18.6%/1000, party=4 33.2%/1000. Fully deterministic per seed (confirmed by re-running the identical sweep multiple times with identical results). Isolated whether toolkit obstacles (BlocksLoS=true for 5/6 refs) help or hurt: a same-seed sweep with Regions[].Obstacles forced nil failed MUCH more often (282/300) than with the real obstacles left in place (20/300) -- obstacles create extra hiding geometry the empty floor lacks, so #694's obstacle consumption is a net IMPROVEMENT over toolkit-dimensions-with-no-obstacles, just not a full fix versus rpg-api's OLD oversized 20/6/14 literal (0/300 over the same trials). Filed rpg-api#696 with full measurements/root-cause/remedy options -- deliberately NOT fixed in this branch: the fix requires either a rpg-toolkit dimension change (out of #694's 'no toolkit source changes' boundary) or a deliberate rpg-api product-tuning decision (memberSightRange/goblinsPerRegion recalibration, or a placement-retry mechanism) beyond #694's stated scope (obstacle consumption only) and rpg-toolkit#826's own issue explicitly lists monster seeding (#689) as out of scope. Chose known-good explicit seeds (verified against the measured bad-seed set) for every new/modified test in this branch that needs an explicit seed, so this branch's OWN test suite is deterministic-green; pre-existing entropy-seeded tests elsewhere in the repo (abandon_encounter_test.go, integration suite, handler-level tests) are unaffected by any file this branch touches but are newly exposed to this same collision -- documented, not silently patched.
